description: Extend the existing controller tests to exercise the new centralized error handling for every endpoint, and add a dedicated test for the GlobalExceptionHandler. Because the controller tests use MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(...), the advice must be explicitly registered via .setControllerAdvice(new GlobalExceptionHandler()) so the tests exercise the real handler. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Update src/test/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/adapter/rest/WalletControllerTest.java: in @Before setup(), register the advice: mockMvc = MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(new WalletController(walletService, new WalletMapperImpl())).setControllerAdvice(new es.jguimar.tinybankAPI.infrastructure.exception.GlobalExceptionHandler()).build(). Keep existing passing tests. Add tests covering: PUT /wallet/{id}/money when walletService.putMoney throws ResourceNotFoundException -> status().isNotFound() and jsonPath('$.status').value(404) and a non-empty $.message; PUT /wallet/{id}/money with missing 'amount' body -> status().isBadRequest(); POST /wallet/money-tranfer when walletService.transferMoney throws ResourceNotFoundException -> isNotFound(); POST /wallet/money-tranfer with an invalid body (e.g. missing walletSource) -> isBadRequest(); a happy-path putMoney and transfer if convenient. Follow the existing given(...).willThrow(...) / willReturn(...) Mockito style. Replace the '//TODO: End up more test cases for all endpoints' comment.

Update src/test/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/adapter/rest/UserControllerTest.java: register the advice the same way in setup() (standaloneSetup(new UserController(userService, new UserMapperImpl())).setControllerAdvice(new GlobalExceptionHandler()).build()). Verify the existing duplicate-user test still asserts status().isConflict() and add assertions that the JSON body carries $.status == 409 and a non-empty $.message. Fix the pre-existing 'createNewUserWrongInput_shouldReturnKO' test which currently stubs willThrow(ResourceExistsException) even though it sends a body missing 'name' (validation fires before the service is called) - the stub is misleading; keep the isBadRequest() expectation but the assertion should reflect a validation 400 body ($.status == 400).

Add a focused unit test src/test/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/infrastructure/exception/GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.java that instantiates GlobalExceptionHandler directly and, for each handler method, passes a mocked javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest (Mockito mock returning a sample URI/method) plus a representative exception, then asserts the returned ResponseEntity has the expected HttpStatus and that the ErrorResponseDto body has matching status/path/non-null message. Cover ResourceNotFoundException(404), ResourceExistsException(409), a Spring Security AccessDeniedException(403), and the catch-all Exception(500) verifying the 500 body message is the generic one (does not equal the raw exception message).

Keep JUnit 4 + Mockito + SpringRunner conventions (this project is JUnit 4.12; do not introduce JUnit 5). Use org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath for body assertions.
acceptance_criteria: WalletControllerTest and UserControllerTest register the GlobalExceptionHandler via setControllerAdvice in setup().

There are tests asserting: not-found (404) for putMoney and transfer, validation (400) for malformed putMoney and transfer bodies, conflict (409) for duplicate user, each also asserting the JSON error body carries the correct $.status and a non-empty $.message.
GlobalExceptionHandlerTest directly verifies status codes and body contents for not-found (404), conflict (409), access-denied (403) and the catch-all (500, generic message).
Tests would fail if FEAT-001's handler were reverted (e.g. bare ResponseStatusException with no body would fail the $.status/$.message assertions), so they meaningfully exercise the new code path.
All tests use JUnit 4 APIs consistent with the existing suite.
verification: Preferred (requires network + JDK 11): from tiny-bank/, run 'JAVA_HOME=/root/.local/share/mise/installs/java/11.0.2 ./gradlew test' and confirm all tests pass. BLOCKED in the current sandbox (no Gradle distribution / dependency cache / registry access).

Sandbox fallback: syntactically validate the test files, confirm they reference GlobalExceptionHandler and ErrorResponseDto correctly, use only JUnit 4 / Mockito / MockMvc APIs already used elsewhere in the suite, and that the standaloneSetup registers the advice.
findings: Implemented all three steps. (1) WalletControllerTest: registered the advice via standaloneSetup(...).setControllerAdvice(new GlobalExceptionHandler()).build(); kept the 4 existing tests; replaced the '//TODO' comment with new cases: putMoney happy-path (200), putMoney ResourceNotFoundException (404 + $.status==404 + $.message isNotEmpty), putMoney missing 'amount' body (400 + $.status==400 + $.message isNotEmpty), transfer happy-path (200), transfer ResourceNotFoundException (404 + body assertions), transfer missing 'walletSource' body (400 + body assertions). Used Mockito anyString()/anyDouble() and put()/post() request builders. (2) UserControllerTest: registered the advice the same way; added $.status==409 + $.message isNotEmpty to the duplicate-user test; fixed createNewUserWrongInput_shouldReturnKO by removing the misleading willThrow(ResourceExistsException) stub (validation fires before the service is called) and asserting the validation 400 body ($.status==400, $.message isNotEmpty). (3) Added GlobalExceptionHandlerTest that instantiates the handler directly, passes a Mockito-mocked HttpServletRequest returning a sample URI/method, and asserts status + ErrorResponseDto body for ResourceNotFoundException(404), ResourceExistsException(409), Spring Security AccessDeniedException(403), and catch-all RuntimeException(500) verifying the 500 body message is the generic one (assertNotEquals raw exception message). Used '$.message' via MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath(...).isNotEmpty() for non-empty message assertions (cleaner than a hamcrest matcher and native to MockMvc). Kept JUnit 4.12 + Mockito + SpringRunner throughout; no JUnit 5 introduced. VALIDATION: './gradlew build' and './gradlew test' could NOT be run in this sandbox - confirmed the Gradle 6.8.3 wrapper dist is only a .part/.lck (incomplete), there is no ~/.gradle/caches dependency store, and services.gradle.org returns HTTP 000 (blocked). This is the documented environment constraint, not a code failure. Validated by careful syntactic review: files use only JUnit4/Mockito/MockMvc/hamcrest APIs already used in the existing suite, reference GlobalExceptionHandler methods (handleResourceNotFound/handleResourceExists/handleAccessDenied/handleGeneric) and ErrorResponseDto getters (getStatus/getPath/getMessage) correctly, and standaloneSetup registers the advice so the tests exercise the real handler. Real build/test verification must be deferred to a networked JDK 11 environment (JAVA_HOME=/root/.local/share/mise/installs/java/11.0.2 ./gradlew test).
